title: Staged Handover Protocol for Deferred Canary and Surge Fallback
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Introduces a staged handover protocol and controller improvements to support deferred canary activations and a surge-fallback routing mode. This PR enables a handover window where: (1) a canary is created but traffic is not immediately shifted; (2) observational checks run on mirrored traffic; (3) on explicit handover the controller performs a coordinated swap with a graceful ramp; (4) if capacity pressure or latency regressions are detected, traffic is routed to pre-configured surge variants until remediation. Motivation: Customers asked for a way to perform canaries that collect live shadow metrics before affecting production traffic and to have a predictable fallback path when capacity or latency regressions happen during rollouts (see ENG-1987). Key changes: new CRD fields for RolloutSpec.stagedHandover (graceWindowSeconds, deferredActivation, surgeVariants, maxSurgePct), a handoff protocol implemented in controllers/handover/handshake.go, a surge-aware router in scheduler/surge_router.go, updates to the simulation harness and integration test cases. Checklist: - [x] API: CRD + validation - [x] Controller: staged handover state machine + leader election guards - [x] Router: surge fallback path and capacity probing - [x] Tests: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests exercising deferred activation and surge fallback - [x] Docs: rollout CRD examples and console doc strings - [x] Migration notes and compatibility checks Behavior notes: - Deferred canary: when deferredActivation=true, controller will create the canary ReplicaSet and mirror traffic but will not increase live traffic until an explicit Handover event (via API or Linear-triggered automation). - Handover arbitration: a three-way handshake ensures only one controller instance completes the final swap (prevents split-brain). - Surge fallback: on sustained latency regressions or soft OOM/queue pressure the scheduler will divert a configurable percentage of traffic to a higher-capacity variant or a pre-warmed fallback pool. - Observability: emits rollout.handover.* and scheduler.surge.* metrics; exposes handover.trace_id in traces. Backwards compatibility: CRD fields are additive and default to conservative behavior (deferredActivation=false, maxSurgePct=0). Migration: existing rollouts unaffected until customers opt-in. Rollout runbooks updated in docs/rollouts/staged-handover.md.

release_notes: Add staged handover protocol: opt-in deferred canaries, surge fallback routing and metrics. CRD additive; no automatic changes for existing rollouts. See docs/rollouts/staged-handover.md for example configs.
testing: Unit: 58 new unit tests covering handshake transitions, surge routing logic, validation. Integration: new scenario that mirrors traffic for 5 minutes in deferred mode and then triggers handover; asserts zero error-traffic during mirror window and correct ramp behavior. Load tests: synthetic workload with ramp to 2x baseline to validate surgeVariants behavior. CI included 2x retries for flaky integration steps and artifacts uploaded to GCS (gs://redwood-ci/pr-99123).
migration_steps: 1) Deploy controller v1.45 which includes CRD and controller code. 2) Optional: update rollout YAMLs to include stagedHandover config. 3) If using console, update client to read handover.trace_id field. 4) For automated handovers via Linear, add an automation webhook that POSTs to /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/handover. No DB migrations required.
rationale: Deferred canaries reduce blast radius by allowing live shadowing before any production traffic shift. Surge fallback provides predictable availability under transient capacity pressure without aborting a rollout or requiring manual intervention. The handshake avoids split-brain and ensures leader safety in HA controller deployments; the design favors observability and debuggability over speculative optimistic swaps.
